summary: Rework of task 9.3 (v1.1 Phase 9, ADR-016 clauses 3, 4, and 5 first bullet) adding the administrator-visible rejection surfacing required by the rework and recorded in the new ADR-021. Attempt 1's correct behaviour is retained: Plugin.UpdateConfiguration overrides BasePlugin<PluginConfiguration>.UpdateConfiguration, calls base, then ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace; a valid candidate activates the running public snapshot and private secret generation atomically without a host restart; an invalid candidate is rejected with the last valid snapshot and private secrets retained, the last valid configuration restored as active and persisted (closing S-9.2-03), the bounded secret-free result retained on Plugin.LastConfigurationValidationResult, service-resolution/validation/notification failures contained, and no custom configuration-save route added. Added: the rejection is now written as exactly one administrator-visible host activity-log entry. The host coupling is isolated behind the plugin-owned IConfigurationRejectionNotifier interface (Jellyfin-free contract: NotifyRejected(IReadOnlyList<string> reasons)); JellyfinConfigurationRejectionNotifier resolves the pinned MediaBrowser.Model.Activity.IActivityManager lazily from the host service provider and writes a Jellyfin.Database.Implementations.Entities.ActivityLog entry with a fixed Name and Type (ArrTagsConfigurationRejected), UserId = Guid.Empty, LogSeverity = Warning, and an Overview/ShortOverview built only from bounded, secret-free validation reasons (at most 8, each reason and every field truncated to the ActivityLog column bounds 512/256). The write is a bounded synchronous wait (WaitAsync 5s + GetAwaiter().GetResult(), consistent with the OnUninstalling drain) and is fully contained; a valid save writes no entry. IConfigurationRejectionNotifier is registered in ArrTagsServiceRegistrator via TryAddSingleton. The pinned Jellyfin.Database.Implementations compile reference flows transitively through Jellyfin.Model (Jellyfin.Model -> Jellyfin.Data -> Jellyfin.Database.Implementations), so no explicit PackageReference was needed; the plugin does not ship it (ExcludeAssets=runtime), matching ADR-015. Research confirmed the exact pinned API and bounds and is recorded in docs/research/jellyfin-expert/configuration-save-failure-surfacing.json. Docs: new ADR-021; ADR-016 clause-4 pointer and References; docs/limitations.md SEC-9 plus a scoping note on SEC-5 (not the full SEC-5 rewrite, which is task 10.3); architecture section 6; data-model 3.12; changelog; PLANS task 9.3 status; project-status; implementation-readiness; README. No post-save reconciliation trigger (task 9.4) was implemented.

known_limitations: The rejected save's HTTP response is still 204 NoContent and the dashboard reports success. Exact behaviour: the supported PluginsController POST calls the void UpdateConfiguration and unconditionally returns 204, so the rejection is surfaced only as the activity-log entry and, on reload, because the last valid configuration is restored. Precondition: the supported save path. Consequence: the administrator sees the rejection in Dashboard -> Activity (or on the next page load), not inline or as an HTTP error; this is the ADR-021 decision and adds no custom route or HTTP error.

Duplicate consecutive identical activity entries are not suppressed. Exact behaviour: each rejected save writes one entry even when it repeats the previous rejection. Precondition: repeated invalid saves by the administrator. Consequence: repeated identical entries in the Activity log; ADR-021 clause 6 defers suppression because admin-initiated saves are infrequent and suppression would add cross-save state to a best-effort path.

The activity-log write is best-effort. Exact behaviour: if IActivityManager cannot be resolved or CreateAsync fails or exceeds the 5-second bounded wait, no entry is written. Precondition: a host activity-manager failure or a slow database. Consequence: the rejection and the last-valid retention still hold and nothing is thrown, but the administrator is not notified of that particular rejection.

base.UpdateConfiguration is not wrapped. Exact behaviour: exceptions raised by the host's own base implementation (for example an I/O failure in SaveConfiguration) propagate unchanged, as they would without the override. Precondition: a failure inside the host base method. Consequence: the plugin-added activation and notification logic never throws, but the host's pre-existing base behaviour is preserved.

Some singleton services capture OperationalLimits at construction (StateRepository: render work-cache TTL/quota and terminal-provenance retention; JellyfinArtworkImageAccess/ArtworkSourceReader/ArtworkPublisher: artifact-size/decode limits), so those particular limit values change only after a host restart. This is a pre-existing Phase 1/6 detail outside the 9.3 acceptance criteria; per-operation resolution was verified for queue capacity/in-flight, provider/render concurrency, metadata freshness, badge definitions, and the renderer output policy.
The bounded post-save reconciliation trigger (task 9.4) is not implemented; existing posters re-render only on the next library event, webhook, post-scan, or scheduled run.

Host-guarded tests (JellyfinHostFact) remain skipped because ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR is unset (63 skips, identical to the pre-task baseline); the live pinned-host activity-log confirmation remains owned by the documented live-verification tasks.
